Th ough covered in armored plates and wielding sword-like claws, the korruk looks almost apologetic in the way it carries itself. Th is 
mammal digs deep into the dry soil of the Grayfynn plains during the heat of the day digging for deep rooted plants and, at night, 
moves slowly above ground for fresher fare. Evidence of its passing is clear for most predators, a long dragging tail that often leads 
to a massive hole in the earth. When found underground, the rather docile looking mammal can turn surprisingly aggressive. When 
cornered, the korruk raises its dermal plates in a threatening display and will ferociously slash with its stone breaking claws, capable of 
cutting through flesh with devastating ease.

korruk, usually consisting of three to four mating pairs and

into the dry earth for tubers, upturning swaths of soil in search
